text:
Sophia (customer): Hey, hitting huge latency spikes from your hosted API since ~09:10 UTC. p95 went from ~120ms to ~2.2s and p99 ~8s. Examples: request_id=abc123, model=rwft-7b, region=us-west1. Can you investigate?
Maya (support): Thanks Sophia — opening an investigation. Can you paste a curl request that reproduces and one request_id from a slow call?
Sophia (customer): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rwft-7b","input":"short prompt"}'
Sophia (customer): slow request_id=abc123, latency=8.3s, status=200 but tokens delayed (streaming gaps).
Maya (support): @Jon can you triage? Looks like queueing/backpressure from symptoms. :eyes:
Jon (eng-oncall): On it. Pulling traces and admission metrics for us-west1. Any service errors or increased 429s?
Maya (support): Not seeing 5xx, mostly successful but slow and long queue wait times. No billing/auth issues reported by customer.
DeployBot: Automatically created incident INC-2026-709 (priority P2) for thread 1801234567.
Jon (eng-oncall): Lee, can you pull worker queue lengths and admission_control logs for the dedicated pool serving rwft-7b in us-west1? Steps I'm running: 1) query metrics: admission_queue_length{region="us-west1",model="rwft-7b"} 2) check per-instance concurrency.
Lee (eng-sre): I see a sharp rise in admission_queue_length around 09:08 UTC — sustained. Per-instance concurrency at cap (64). We also have a subset of pods reporting high GC/CPU on GPU host. P95 token latency correlates with queue wait time. Snippet from logs: 
```
[09:09:02] admission: enqueue req=abc123 queue_len=78
[09:09:02] worker-07: serving req=abc123 state=queued
[09:09:03] admission: dequeue req=abc123 worker=worker-07 kernel_wait=0.002s kv_miss=true
[09:09:11] worker-07: generate: start seq=0
[09:09:20] worker-07: generate: flush seq=0 total_tokens=48
```
Lee (eng-sre): Looks like backlog + a hot set of long-running requests (large context / long outputs) are saturating concurrency and causing admission waiting.
Arjun (eng-runtime): We also have a deployment change at 08:50 rolling out a memory-opt patch to rwft-7b which reduced batch sizes — that may have inadvertently increased per-request latency under load. Related change: reduce_batch_ms was set from 12 -> 6 in runtime config.
Jon (eng-oncall): That would lower batching, increasing per-token overhead and increasing number of in-flight requests — combined with concurrency cap leads to longer queueing. Good find. Immediate mitigations: 
- revert reduce_batch_ms to 12 for us-west1 rwft-7b (temporary)
- bump per-pool concurrency from 64 -> 96 for 15m window
- enable emergency-burst capacity for rwft-7b (allow additional prewarmed instances)

Lee (eng-sre): I'll run the concurrency bump and enable burst. Command I'm running: 
```
# temporary concurrency bump
kubectl -n inference set env ds/rwft-7b CONCURRENCY_LIMIT=96 --overwrite
# enable burst capacity (platform toggle)
platformctl capacity toggle --pool rwft-7b-us-west1 --burst true --reason "P95 spike 2026-03-15"
```
Maya (support): Noted. I'll tell customer we're applying mitigations and to expect improvement in ~5-10 minutes.
Ravi (eng-platform): Heads up — increasing concurrency may raise CPU/GPU memory pressure; monitoring dashboards set. Also enabling fallback routing to rwft-7b-quantized variant if queue_len > 50 for >2m.
Jon (eng-oncall): Also recommended: temporary routing policy to divert new traffic to us-central1 and eu-west1 where capacity is plentiful. I can flip the route if needed.
Sophia (customer): Thanks — saw p95 drop from ~2.2s to ~240ms after 7m. p99 still ~1.1s but improving. Will let you know if it regresses. :thumbsup:
Lee (eng-sre): Monitoring shows queue_len back to baseline and per-instance cpu/gpu usage stabilized. Root cause hypothesis: runtime config change reduced batching and increased in-flight requests while a subset of pods experienced elevated GPU stalls (driver soft faults) — together produced admission pileup.
Arjun (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: revert runtime patch to a canary with adjusted reduce_batch_ms=10 and add auto-tune logic to increase batch window under high QPS. Will create RFC for tuning heuristics.
Maya (support): Closing loop with Sophia: we'll keep the incident open for 24h and reach out if any regression. Any action items?
Lee (eng-sre): Action items (assign): 1) Arjun — RFC + canary (due EOD). 2) Ravi — add an SLO alert that triggers when admission_queue_length>50 for >2m (due today). 3) Jon — document emergency routing playbook (due tomorrow).
Jon (eng-oncall): I'll also add a retro note in postmortems channel once we validate root cause.
Sophia (customer): Appreciate the quick response — latency back to acceptable.
Maya (support): Thanks all. Marking thread as monitored. :white_check_mark:
